title: SSE midstream mismatch: multipath session recovery and partial output reconciliation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple customers reported truncated streaming responses and duplicate token segments when clients reconnected after transient network failures. Tangled routing across edge proxies and backend handoffs produce multipath fragments that the current resume protocol cannot deterministically reconcile, causing partial outputs, out-of-order tokens, or silent truncation. This ticket coordinates an MVP fix (session-level checkpointing + fragment attribution headers) and an operational playbook for escalations. Scope covers Hosted API (primary), with compatibility notes for Dedicated and Private deployments. Impact: production user-facing truncations and duplicated tokens for long-running generations (> 30s) under intermittent edge disconnects.

2026-03-12 - Lina Wong (SRE): Observed edge LB retries correlate with duplicate fragment arrival. Proposed a deterministic dedupe window and idempotency token to be emitted by the runtime.
2026-03-12 - PM feedback (Marco Liu): Prioritize customer-facing mitigations first: server-side keepalive/close semantics and an SDK patch that surfaces ambiguous final_token warnings to customers.
2026-03-13 - Diego Romero: RFC posted for the checkpoint header, fragment attribution fields, and deterministic merge algorithm. Linked PR for runtime changes and SDK patch in links below.

2026-03-14 - QA (Maya Singh): Integration test harness created to simulate 3-edge multipath reroute; initial results show 95% success in stitch, remaining failures due to late final-token marker loss. Next: gap-fill backfill protocol.

steps_repro: 1) Start a long-running streaming generation (> 30s) using Hosted API SSE from behind a corporate proxy.
2) Introduce a transient network flap on client side or trigger LB path change at the edge at t+12s.
3) Force the edge to retry to alternate backend host, creating two overlapping partial streams.
4) Observe client receives duplicated segments and a truncated final token or missing EOS marker.
5) Reproduce locally with integration harness and CHAOS mode to validate counts of duplicate/wrong-order fragments.
root_cause: Edge load balancer retries combined with backend handoff semantics can produce overlapping stream fragments that lack a stable global sequence marker. Our resume protocol assumes single linear checkpoint per session; it does not attribute fragments with a stable session+path id, so late-arriving fragments are sometimes applied incorrectly or discarded, causing duplicates or truncation.
fix_plan: A) Introduce session-checkpoint header (x-rw-session-checkpoint) emitted every N tokens by the runtime with monotonically increasing checkpoint id.
B) Add fragment attribution headers (x-rw-fragment-id, x-rw-fragment-parent-checkpoint) so the client/SDK can deterministically order and dedupe fragments.
C) Implement server-side merge algorithm that accepts out-of-order fragments within a bounded window and uses checkpoint id to seal continuity.
D) SDK patch: surface ambiguous-final-token warnings and auto-request backfill when stitchable gaps are detected.
E) Short-term mitigation: SRE to adjust edge retry window and enable stronger keepalive (reduce silent disconnects).
rollout_plan: 1) Merge runtime change behind feature flag 'multipath-stitch-v1' (canary in us-west-2).
2) Deploy SDK patch to beta channel and notify pilot customers to opt-in (Client opt-in required for backfill).
3) Monitor canary metrics for duplicated-fragment-rate, truncated-response-rate, final-token-loss-rate for 48h.
4) If metrics drop >= 90% and no regression in latency P50/P95, gradually enable for 25%->50%->100% over 48h.
5) Post-rollout: enable server-side merge globally and remove feature flag after 1 week of stable metrics.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Canary usage shows >= 90% reduction in truncated-response incidents for canary tenants compared to baseline.
2) No more than 2% increase in P95 token-latency induced by merge algorithm under normal load.
3) SDK surface shows explicit ambiguous-final-token events for customers when backfill is required.
4) Support playbook updated and customers on active escalations verified fixes in their environment.
5) Unit/integration tests covering multipath reassembly added to CI.
notes: Operational trade-offs: aggressive dedupe window reduces false duplicates but may increase latency while waiting for late fragments; we choose a 250ms window for canary and will tune based on p95 token latency.
Compatibility: Dedicated and Private runtimes share the same resume semantics; plan to ship header-based protocol as opt-in config until Private deployments synchronize runtime versions.
Follow-ups: separate ticket to add per-tenant circuit breaker for noisy clients (post-merge).
Escalation playbook: support should enable keepalive and advise client SDK upgrade as immediate steps; provide scoped logs (session-id) for any remaining cases.
